items.title: Mayor Says Land Appraisal Puts Glenforest Youth Hub Agreement at Risk
items.summary: According to Mayor Alvin Tedjo, a $6 million youth hub planned for Mississauga's east end is now at risk of delay or cancellation after a recent appraisal altered the financials behind the project. Tedjo and Ward 3 Coun. Chris Fonseca said in a letter to provincial Education Minister Paul Calandra that the Glenforest Youth Hub, planned for a site at Glenforest Secondary School, was in advanced stages and only weeks away from receiving a full building permit. The city has already invested roughly $3 million in design and development work, the letter said. The project was meant to build on the success of the Malton Youth Hub, which has operated since late 2023. Tedjo and Fonseca said the city remains committed to working with the education ministry, the school board and other stakeholders to find a mutually beneficial solution.

items.title: Peel Police Say Carjacking and Crash Investigation Led to Assault-Style Rifle Seizure
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, two 18-year-old men were charged after a break-in and crash in Mississauga that ended with officers seizing an assault-style firearm. Police say the incident began on Feb. 18, 2025, when a resident reported a break-in by four suspects and gave officers a description of the getaway vehicle. Officers were later contacted about a crash involving the same vehicle at Glen Erin Drive and the Collegeway, police say. Police shared video showing officers arriving at the crash scene, where the vehicle had suffered severe front-end damage and come to rest in a snowbank. Investigators say the suspects carjacked a victim at gunpoint and stole the victim's vehicle shortly after the break-in, and the Central Robbery Bureau's investigation led to the recovery of the firearm and an arrest.

items.title: Mississauga Residents Worry New Mayor's Advisory Committee Overhaul Could Limit Public Input
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Mayor Alvin Tedjo is bringing a motion to his first council meeting as mayor to consolidate several city advisory committees into three new ones. The motion proposes that each new committee include two council members and six citizen or business members with expertise in that committee's area of focus. Once the new committees are appointed, the existing advisory committees will be retired, according to the motion. Some residents say the change could reduce opportunities for public input on municipal decision-making, since resident representation on each committee would be limited to six members. The proposal is scheduled to come before council at its first meeting of the new term.

items.title: Peel Officer Testifies He Fired on Instinct, Not Decision, Before Fatal Francique Shooting
items.summary: According to testimony at the coroner's inquest into the death of Jamal Francique, Peel Regional Police Const. Milan Ivkovic said he did not make a conscious decision to fire his gun but acted out of a fight-or-flight instinct during the January 2020 arrest attempt. Ivkovic was part of a team of plainclothes officers in unmarked vehicles who sought to arrest Francique near his home over an alleged bail breach, the inquest heard. Officers had planned to stop Francique before he reached his car, but he moved faster than expected and the blocking vehicle arrived late, according to testimony. Ivkovic testified that Francique's car suddenly reversed and lurched toward him as he stepped onto the curb, prompting him to fire four times toward where a driver would be. A lawyer for Francique's father suggested under cross-examination that Ivkovic should have moved out of the way instead.

items.title: Port Credit's Light Up the Port Festival Returns Saturday With New Interactive Light Structures
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Port Credit's Light Up the Port festival returns this Saturday, Nov. 28, from 4 p.m. to 9 p.m. at Port Credit Memorial Park, with free holiday entertainment, music, shopping and family activities. This year's event adds six towering, illuminated musical structures that light up and play sound when stepped on, created in partnership with Visit Mississauga. The annual Christmas tree lighting takes place at 6 p.m., officially opening the holiday season, and the Port Credit Lighthouse will also be lit in colour for the occasion. Families can get free photos with Santa and ride the PC Polar Express, a trackless train inspired by the holiday film. The event is free to attend, according to the outlet.

items.title: Mississauga Pauses Large-Scale Data Centre Development While It Studies Planning Rules
items.summary: According to city officials, Mississauga has temporarily paused approval of new large-scale data centre development while it studies how future projects should be planned and managed. The city says it is inviting community members to learn about its data centre policy review and get involved, as the rapid growth of artificial intelligence drives rising demand for data centres across North America. Data centres are being proposed and built in many towns and cities across the continent to support that growth, officials noted. Cities cannot automatically stop development from happening, but they can set rules for how it occurs, officials said. The review will draw on input from partner agencies, other levels of government and members of the public, according to the city's notice to residents.

items.title: Slim Third-Ballot Win Makes Navdeep Bains the New Ontario Liberal Leader
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, former Mississauga and Brampton MP Navdeep Bains has won the Ontario Liberal Party leadership, prevailing by a narrow margin in a third round of voting on Nov. 21. The party says more than 20,500 members cast ballots, a 15 per cent increase in turnout from the previous leadership race. Bains spent years moving between federal politics, teaching and the private sector before entering the provincial race. In a statement following the result, Bains said he was honoured by the trust Ontario Liberals placed in him and declared the party ready for what he called Ontario's moment.

items.title: Mississauga's Election Sign Ban Faces Charter Challenge As Rights Group Intervenes
items.summary: According to the Canadian Constitution Foundation, the group has been granted leave to intervene in a court challenge against the City of Mississauga's total ban on election signs on public property. The case was brought by longtime political candidate Greg Vezina, whose campaign signs were removed from public property under the city's by-law in 2019. Vezina argues the by-law is a content-based restriction, since the city allows other signs, such as those advertising housing developments and farmers' markets, while banning only election signs. His application will proceed to a hearing at the Superior Court of Justice over whether the ban violates free expression under the Charter. CCF interim litigation director Josh Dehaas said sign bans disadvantage lesser known candidates, since signs are one of the few affordable ways to reach voters against established politicians.

items.title: Toronto Police Say Mississauga Man Used Fake Badge to Pose as Officer at Etobicoke Park
items.summary: According to Toronto Police, a Mississauga man employed as a correctional officer at the Toronto South Detention Centre is accused of posing as a police officer during an encounter at Colonel Sam Smith Park in Etobicoke this past Sunday. Police say the man approached occupants of a vehicle in the parking lot, identified himself as an Ontario Provincial Police officer and displayed a metal badge. He then demanded identification from the occupants and directed them to exit the vehicle, according to police. Responding officers located a suspect near the scene shortly afterward, police said in a news release. Joshia Jiju Koshy, 21, of Mississauga, was arrested and charged, and is scheduled to appear at the Ontario Court of Justice in Toronto on Feb. 16, 2027.

items.title: Mississauga Budget Committee Set to Weigh MiWay Fare Hike This Week
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga's budget committee will consider a proposal this week to raise MiWay transit fares starting Jan. 1, 2027. Senior city staff are recommending the increase to help offset rising costs tied to inflation, labour, maintenance and service delivery, according to a report set for Wednesday's meeting. The report notes MiWay still faces a revenue shortfall despite previous fare adjustments. Sam Rogers, the city's commissioner of transportation and works, said in the report that the proposed changes reflect a balanced approach to current revenue and ridership realities. City councillors are expected to debate the recommendation before any fare changes take effect.
